Creating your video. Please wait a moment.

Most messaging and social apps re-encode videos to save data, which lowers the quality. To keep the original quality, send the file itself, for example through a file manager, a cloud drive, or Wi-Fi transfer in Tools.

" Apps and services that protect their content, such as streaming services and banking apps, tell Android to block screen capture. The recording comes out black by design, and this cannot be bypassed.
Some apps block capture on a single screen only, for example a payment or password screen, so only part of your video is black.
"If the app you recorded does not protect its content:" - Check whether the video plays on the editing page. If it does, close other apps and restart AZ Screen Recorder.
- Lower "Resolution and Video quality" in Settings, then record again.
- If the problem continues, restart your device. "

- Some apps and older devices cannot play video recorded at a high frame rate or a high resolution. Record at a lower Frame rate and Resolution, or run the file through Compress video in Tools" before sharing.
- If the recording was interrupted, the file may be damaged. See the question about corrupted videos. "

"- Internal audio needs Android 10 or later. On Android 9 and earlier the option is not shown, because the system does not offer audio capture at all.
- Even on Android 10 and later, each app decides whether other apps may record its sound. Many streaming and music apps, and some games, opt out. When that happens the capture is silent and no screen recorder can change it.
- Set "Audio source to Internal audio and microphone" instead. The microphone picks up what your speaker plays, so the video keeps its audio.
- Internal audio captures media and game audio. System sounds such as notification tones, alarms and calls are not included. "

" - The file may be larger than the app you are sharing to accepts. Size limits differ for every app and platform.
- Use "Compress video in Tools" to make the file smaller, or trim it in the video editor.
- To send the original file at full quality, use "Wi-Fi transfer in Tools or upload it to a cloud drive.

If a recording was interrupted, for example by a crash or by the battery running out, the file can be left unplayable. AZ Screen Recorder marks it as Corrupted video" in your video list.
- Tap the corrupted video and choose "Repair".
- Repair needs a reference video: a working recording made with the same resolution, frame rate and quality settings. If you do not have one, record a short clip with the same settings first.
- Repair recovers as much as it can. The result is not always perfect. "

" - The system can close the bubble when memory is low. Close apps you are not using, or restart your device.
- Check that "Display over other apps" is still allowed for AZ Screen Recorder in your system settings. Some battery saving tools revoke it.
- Open Settings and tap "Avoid unexpected stop" so the system does not shut the app down in the background.
- You can always start and stop recording from the notification. "

- Open Settings and turn on Hide floating bubble during recording". The bubble is hidden while you record and comes back when you stop.
- Turn on "Magic button: invisible control" to keep an invisible control on screen instead. Tap it to pause or resume, long press to stop.
- You can also start and stop recording from the notification. "

" Yes. What you record stays on your device.
- Recordings and screenshots are saved to your device storage. We never upload them, and we cannot see them.
- "Auto Caption" transcribes on your device. Your audio is never sent to a server. The app downloads a speech model once, and after that captions work offline.
- Android shows a screen sharing notification for as long as recording is active, so it is always clear when the screen is being captured. "

" Subscriptions are handled by Google Play, not inside AZ Screen Recorder.
- Open Google Play, tap your profile icon, then "Payments and subscriptions and Subscriptions".
- Select AZ Screen Recorder to change or cancel your plan.
- Cancelling stops the next renewal. Pro stays active until the end of the period you already paid for.
- A lifetime purchase is a one time payment. It never renews and there is nothing to cancel. "

" Pro belongs to the Google account that made the purchase, not to the device.
- Open Google Play, tap your profile icon, and check that you are signed in with the account you used to buy Pro. If several accounts are signed in, Pro is only restored for the account that paid.
- On the upgrade screen, open the menu and tap "Already upgraded?"
- If you bought a subscription, check that it is still active in Google Play under "Payments and subscriptions".
- Restart your device after switching accounts.
- If Pro is still missing, write to az.screen.recorder@gmail.com with the order number from your Google Play receipt. "

Android 10 and later" - Set "Audio source to Internal audio" to record what the device plays, including sound sent to your earphones.
- Set "Audio source to Internal audio and microphone" to record the device audio and your own voice together.
"Android 9 and earlier" - Only microphone recording is available. The microphone cannot hear audio sent to your earphones, so unplug or disconnect them if you need the device sound in the video. "

Phone calls and video calls" - Android gives call audio and the microphone to the calling app and blocks other apps from capturing them. No screen recorder can record a call with sound.
"Meeting apps such as Zoom or Google Meet" - If you only need to watch, join with your microphone muted, set "Audio source to Internal audio and microphone", and keep the meeting on the speaker so the microphone can pick it up.
- If the meeting app handles the session as a call, Android will still block the capture and the video will be silent.
"The reliable way" - Record the meeting with a second device, or use the recording feature built into the meeting app. "

" - Your recordings always appear in the AZ Screen Recorder video list right away. The system gallery can take a few minutes to index a new file.
- Check "Trash if you may have deleted the video. On Android 11 and later, deleted files are kept there while Use trash" is on.
- Open the folder shown under "Output directory" in Settings with a file manager.
- If you changed the save location to an SD card, the videos are on the SD card and not in internal storage.
- Long recordings are saved in parts, so look for more than one file. "

First check that Audio source in Settings is not set to Mute".
If a finished recording turned out silent, AZ Screen Recorder marks it in your video list. Tap the hint on that video to see what happened.
"The recorded app blocked its audio" - Android lets every app decide whether other apps may capture its sound. Streaming apps, music apps and some games refuse, and the capture comes out silent. No screen recorder can override this.
- Set "Audio source to Internal audio and microphone". The microphone still picks up the sound from your speaker, so the video keeps its audio. Turn the volume up and do not use earphones.
"You were in a call" - Android reserves call audio and the microphone for the calling app, so calls cannot be recorded with sound.
"Microphone recording" - Only one app can use the microphone at a time. If a game or a meeting app is holding it, your recording will be silent.
- Make sure nothing is covering the microphone while you record.
- Internal audio needs Android 10 or later. On Android 9 and earlier, only "Microphone is available.

"The orientation is decided when the recording starts and stays the same for the whole video, so turning the device during a recording does not rotate the video.
- With "Orientation set to Auto" in Settings, AZ Screen Recorder uses the orientation your device is in at the moment recording starts. Turn the device first, then start recording.
- You can also set "Orientation to Landscape or Portrait in Settings to fix it yourself, whichever way the device is held.

Check Stop options" in Settings first. A recording ends on its own if any of these is turned on: - "Stop when screen off" - "Stop when shaking device" - "Enable time limit", which stops the recording at the limit you set
Other causes: - You tapped "Stop sharing" in the screen sharing notification or dialog shown by Android. That ends the capture immediately.
- The system stopped the app in the background. Open Settings and tap "Avoid unexpected stop".
- Your device ran out of free storage.
- The device got too hot, so the system throttled the encoder. "

- Lower Resolution, Frame rate and Video quality" in Settings. Recording at the maximum settings can be more than the device can encode in real time.
- Close background apps and keep only AZ Screen Recorder and the app you want to record.
- Turn off battery saver, which slows down the encoder.
- If another app is holding the microphone, set "Audio source to Internal audio", or close that app.
- If the screen stays frozen, restart your device. "

" Yes, on Android 14 and later. Everything outside the app you choose, including your notifications and other apps, stays out of the video.
- Open Settings and turn on "Single-app recording".
- When you start recording, pick the app in the confirmation dialog Android shows.
- If you leave or close the app you picked, Android ends the capture and the recording stops.
- The option is not shown on Android 13 and earlier, because the system does not support it. "

" - Apps that draw over the screen, such as blue light filters and brightness controls, can block the system permission dialog. Turn them off and try again.
- Android asks you to confirm screen capture before recording. You have to tap "Start now. If you tap Cancel", recording does not start.
- You can also start and stop recording from the notification.
- If the button still does not respond, restart AZ Screen Recorder. "

Screen capture confirmation" - Android asks you to confirm before any app may capture the screen. On Android 14 and later this confirmation is required for every single recording and screenshot, which is why you see it each time. It is a system rule and cannot be skipped or remembered.
"Recording notification" - Android shows a notification for the whole time the screen is being captured. It cannot be removed while recording.
"Display over other apps" - This permission is what lets the floating bubble and the recording controls appear on top of other apps. Without it the bubble cannot work.
These prompts are normal Android privacy features. They do not send anything anywhere. "

" - Audio and video drift apart when the device is under heavy load, for example when several apps are running while you record.
- Close background apps, then lower "Resolution and Frame rate" in Settings and record again.
- Choosing a frame rate higher than your screen refresh rate does not help. AZ Screen Recorder already limits recording to what your display supports. "

" Long recordings are saved in parts so that a single file never grows large enough to be rejected by the file system or by other apps.
- A new part starts at about 10 GB when videos are saved to internal storage, and at about 3.5 GB when they are saved to an SD card.
- Nothing is lost. The parts are recorded one after another and all of them appear in your video list.
- You can join them again with "Merge videos in the video editor.

" - This is usually a playback problem rather than a recording problem. Try the video in another player first.
- Restart the app and play the video again.
- Record a short test clip at a lower "Resolution and Video quality". If the test clip looks correct, keep the lower settings.
- If the issue continues, restart your device. "

"- Turn off battery saver or low power mode. These modes slow down the video encoder and can stop a recording.
- Open Settings and tap "Avoid unexpected stop". This lets AZ Screen Recorder keep running when the system tries to restrict it in the background.
- Lower "Resolution, Frame rate and Video quality" in Settings. Recording at the highest settings is more than many devices can encode in real time, and this is the most common cause of a failed recording.
- Close apps you are not recording to free up memory, then start again.
- If another app is holding the microphone, recording can fail to start. Close that app, or set "Audio source to Internal audio".
- Open the screen you want to capture first, then start recording.
- If none of this helps, restart your device and try again. "
